newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: SOCCER-YUGOSLAVIA KEEP PRESSURE ON SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-YUGOSLAVIA KEEP PRESSURE ON SPAIN.

text.p: Yugoslavia kept the pressure on European group six leaders Spain with a 2-0 victory over Slovakia in World Cup qualifier on Sunday.
AC Milan's Dejan Savicevic and Real Madrid's Predrag Mijatovic hit the target to carry Yugoslavia to 19 points in their group, one behind Spain.
Yugoslavia came within a whisker of a fourth minute goal, but Sinisa Mihajlovic's attempted lob over Slovak keeper Ladislav Molnar hit the crossbar.
The Slovaks' tight defence capitulated in the 17th minute when Juventus's Vladimir Jugovic headed a cross from Predrag Mijatovic towards Savicevic, who scored from close range.
Minutes later, Mijatovic shot a powerful left-foot volley straight into Molnar, who made a quick grab for the ball after it bounced off his chest.
Slovakia's only opportunity in the first half came in the 36th minute when Dusan Tittel headed a free kick cross past Ivica Kralj's goal.
Yugoslavia twice came close to scoring directly from corner kicks and missed several other good opportunities.

Their efforts were crowned in the 75th minute -- a cross from Mihajlovic found Mijatovic, who blasted a left footer past a diving Molnar for his sixth goal in Yugoslavia's eight European group six qualifiers.
Spain retained their lead at the top of the group with a 1-0 victory against the Czech Republic.
